answer.evidence: The object is a face-on skeleton: a skull in rows 1-5 (widths 4,6,6,6,4), a 2px neck at row 6, then shoulders and ribs as horizontal stripes. The stripes (light bone, with one dark row at 10, 13, 16, 19, 22, 25) are vertical-face detail with no front-edge line and no eave shadow. The skull is only 6 wide, narrower than the 7-14 wide ribcage and base, so it does not overhang the shaft as a cap plate would. It shows no horizontal surface, only eyes and a face. The base mound in rows 25-29 is dark and drawn as a front face. No part of the column has a top surface, so it reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bone/vertebrae pillar with a skull on top, about one tile wide and 1.5-2 tiles tall. It has 8 visible tones per tile, close to the hedge (9) and below the well (20) and stall (17). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted, not near-black. The bone segments show roughly 4 lightness steps (highlight, light, mid, shadow), a little short of the 5-6 Beodeul uses on its main materials. Segment rings give some texture, but there are no per-bone speckles or grain, and the form is a bit thin and simple next to the well and stall. Overall it is acceptable but slightly less rich than the richest references. Because the guidance says to fail when in doubt, this is a borderline call and I fail it for the slightly shallower ramp and sparse texture.

answer.evidence: This is a skeleton figure seen face-on. A skull (rows 1-5, widths 4-6-6-6-4) narrows to a 2px neck at row 6, then the ribs and arms (rows 7-24) widen to 9-12 px. The skull is narrower than the shaft, so it does not overhang as a cap plate and is a head shape, not an ellipse lid. The ribs are a series of horizontal bands on a vertical face, with no front-edge line or eave shadow marking a horizontal surface. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bone pillar of stacked vertebra and rib segments topped with a skull, and it is narrower and smaller than the references. It has about 8 visible tones per tile, close to the hedge (9) and below the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted (a dark warm-grey or brown beside the bone) and counts as dark_material_tone. The bone ramp has about 4 steps (highlight, light, mid, dark), against 5-6 in the references. Each segment is shaded roughly alike, so it looks somewhat repetitive and lacks the per-stone and per-tile texture of the well and stall. It would sit acceptably next to the references, but it reads a little thinner and simpler than the richest of them. When in doubt, fail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small stacked-vertebrae bone pillar topped with a skull. Its measured facts are 8 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted rather than black. That is in line with prop-hedge (9 tones) but well below prop-well-roofed (20) and prop-stall-cheese (17). By eye the bone ramp has about 4 steps (highlight, light, mid, shadow), with segment shading and a few grain dots but little per-piece texture. It is cleaner and simpler than the richer references, which have more varied materials and fine detail. It is a small, narrow object, so I do not fail it for size alone. Even so, it reads a little thinner and flatter than the Beodeul well and stall, and I would not accept it next to them without more bone grain and a fifth shading step.
